_comment: Vendored canonical outside-agent contract corpus (schemas + conformance vectors + manifest) from Consiliency/spec. This is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH the agent-harness outside-agent validator is tested against, so a silently-drifting copy would recreate agent-harness#371. The drift-guard test recomputes these digests. Update ONLY by re-vendoring from a spec commit and refreshing this record; do not hand-edit vectors to fit the validator (that is the defect, not the fix).
note: Vendored from the immutable annotated tag v0.2.1 (deref commit b862f977) — the SAME anchor EXPECTED_OUTSIDE_AGENT_CONTRACT_PIN records after Consiliency/agent-harness#370. The three digests the pin carries agree with this record byte-for-byte: submission schema 5670b500…, verdict schema 86169277…, vector manifest 78858828…. Keep them in lockstep — a vendored copy older than the pin would mean we validate against a different dialect than we pin to, which is agent-harness#371 in miniature.
oracle_note: oracle/outside_agent_router.py is spec's NORMATIVE executable oracle (route()/blocker_class_of), vendored byte-identically from the SAME v0.2.1 commit (spec blob 667a92f10d49809f84fe48a2aed4bc4752deccee). It is TEST-ONLY: test_outside_agent_corpus_oracle.py uses it as a drift guard proving each vector's manifest expected_verdict/expected_blocker_class is what the oracle actually derives from the vendored payload+schema — so a mutated vector or a wrong declared class fails closed. It is NOT imported by production code and does NOT turn our conformance gate into a router. Its _schema_dir() resolves to _contract/schemas (this dir), so it validates against the SAME vendored schemas, never a re-hosted copy. Do NOT hand-edit; re-vendor from a spec tag and refresh this digest.
